L165: ## Thapra Palace Library
L166: 
L167: In 1976, Silpakorn University inaugurated its inaugural university library at Thapra Palace. Housed within Thapra Palace President's Office, as a divided department of the Central Division, Silpakorn University. The Library shared space with other departments located behind the Silpa Bhirasri statue. At that time, the library's service area was limited to approximately 50 square meters.

L174: ## Sanamchandra Palace Library
L175: Silpakorn University constructed a new library and expanded the campus to Sanamchandra Palace in Nakhon Pathom Province in 1968. Under Sanamchandra Palace President's Office, The library was just a divided department, holding books, an audio library, and audiovisual media and materials. Sanamchandra Palace Library was operating from a temporary office on the ground floor of Tabkaew Building 1 (A1), with a serving area of approximately 200 square meters.
L176: Sanamchandra Palace Library was relocated to a 2-storey building in 1976. Later, the library was relocated to a new 4-storey building, which became the library's current location in 1993. Later, in 2002, Sanamchandra Palace expanded the additional service area to a new structure, M.L.Pin Malakul Building.
L177: 【48†Learn more】
L178: ## Phetchaburi IT Campus Library
L179: Silpakorn University expanded the institution into Petchaburi IT Campus in the Academic Year 2002, in order to give proper schooling as required in the 8th National Education Development Plan, and designed and amended the Phetchaburi IT Campus Master Plan (B.E. 2545-2549). On May 17, 2002, the Central Library established the Phetchaburi IT Campus Library, using the 3rd floor of the school building as an office. Responsible for technological operations and service management at the Thapra Palace Library.
L180: In 2006, the library relocated to the first and second floors of the academic building.

L186: ## Silpakorn University Archives
L187: 
L188: Silpakorn University's Central Library not only offers library services across all three campuses but also manages the Silpakorn University Archives Project, which functions as a department within the university's internal division. This addition to the Central Library's mission was implemented in May 1998, as outlined in the resolution from the Dean's Meeting No. 7/1997.
L189: In accordance with the Dean's Meeting resolution No. 1/2013 on January 9, 2013, and the Silpakorn University Official Announcement on the Establishment and Division of Departments under the Supervision of Silpakorn University (No. 19) in 2013, disclosed on January 9, 2013, the status of the Silpakorn University Archives Project has been upgraded to a department under the Central Library's oversight. It is officially known as "Silpakorn University Archives or SU Archives."

L173: # KMUTNB Central Library
L174: To support studying and teaching activities as well as research and development and to provide the best academic environment for students, the central library of KMUTNB provides access to electronic resources and other library services and includes academic service and facilities such as borrowing and returning books, interlibrary loan and copying, printing etc. The central library provides academic information resources to all faculty, staff and students, as well as to the general public.

L86: T he mission of the Faculty of ICT is to give the best academic support to the students. Thus, we provide up-to-date computer and IT facilities to support students’ academic development and to enhance their learning potential.
L87: A number of servers for both administration and various course projects are also provided. Every room and laboratory has access to the internet through wired and wireless connections. Advanced laboratories for senior students are also set up with modern applications. In addition, every classroom is equipped with a computer, a projector, and a sound system to be used in lecturing, tutoring, and other activities.
L88: Computers are available in several computer labs to support general use and specific class activities. For extracurricular activities, the ICT Grand Auditorium is spacious enough to host large student meetings, academic conferences, and other large-scale events. The multi-purpose “Bits and Bytes” hall is also available to host smaller scale meetings and conferences.
L89: It contains several separate training and meeting rooms including the mini-theatre room which is fully equipped with a state-of-the-art multimedia system.

L115:   * Libraries
L116: Salaya Campus is the hub of the Mahidol University Library and Knowledge Center (MULKC), which contains an extensive collection of over 1,100,000 books, theses, research reports and bound journals, 1,051 printed journals, 39,000 electronic journals, 71,000 electronic books, as well as 20,000 Thai and English-language audio-visual materials. The Central Library has hundreds of computer terminals and multi-media viewing library equipment.
L117: It also offers a full range and specialized services including online reference services, multi-database searching and document delivery services.
L118: There are 25 branch libraries in the Library Automation system. These are located in various academic departments on each campus, but are all connected to the Central Library by the computer database MULINET. The branch libraries maintain extensive book, journal and textbook collections in their respective fields of study and offer a full range of services, including electronic database searching and inter-library loans. Some Faculties and Institutes maintain their own libraries.
L119: These include the largest collection of medical and public health books and periodicals in Thailand.

L32@P0: 1) The Reader Project
L33@P0: The Reader Project, initiated by the National Library of Thailand, aims
L34@P0: to expand access to library resources for library users unable to visit the library
L35@P0: in person. Recognising the physical barriers some individuals face, the project
L36@P0: delivers books directly to users' homes via mail, completely free of charge. This
L37@P0-1: initiative not only bridges the gap for those with physical limitations but also 2
L38@P1: broadens the opportunity for all users to comfortably engage with the library’s
L39@P1: resources from their homes.
L40@P1: 2) Co-Working Spaces
L41@P1: The National Library of Thailand has introduced a newly built coworking space, open for free use by the communities. This effort reflects the
L42@P1: library’s commitment to transforming its space into a versatile and functional
L43@P1: environment, catering to the needs of the communities. By offering this
L44@P1: resource, the library aims to foster a collaborative atmosphere that supports
L45@P1: learning, creativity, and connection within the community.
L46@P1: 3) The NLT Café
L47@P1: The NLT Café is a space deliberately designed to enhance the overall
L48@P1: comfort of the library by providing a relaxed environment where users can enjoy
L49@P1: a drink while reading. The aim is to create a more inviting atmosphere, allowing
L50@P1: visitors to unwind and spend their free time in a comfortable, cozy setting,
L51@P1: making the library experience even more enjoyable.
L52@P1: 4) The NLT Theatre
L53@P1: The National Library of Thailand had renovated the NLT theatre
L54@P1: which was designed for showcasing Thai films. This theatre features classic Thai
L55@P1: films provided by the Film Archive, allowing users to enjoy screens for free. This
L56@P1: aims to enhance cultural appreciation and promote the significance of Thai
L57@P1: cinemas, while also supporting the local movie industry.

L59@P1: In 2023, the library expanded its digital collection by digitizing
L60@P1: approximately 56,000 items, including manuscripts, rare books, old newspapers,
L61@P1: old journals, microfilms, microjackets, and phonograph records.
